Background (from the session that started this one):
On 2026-10-31 Kenneth tried to connect his own Bambu P1S through JusPrin's printer chat on this Mac. The model told him "no printer in LAN mode is on the network" twice and fell back on invented Bambu menu paths, because the app's tools reported nothing about what the network search had actually seen: once no search had run yet, and once the P1S had announced itself in cloud mode 7 seconds before the refusal. A fix session (branch `claude/festive-lederberg-693438`) made `printer_connection_status` report the search state and a `seen` list with reasons such as `cloud_mode`, made `printer_connect` refuse with the facts ("P1s at 192.168.0.198 was seen on the network with LAN Only off"), posts a note to the model when the first printer appears or after 15 seconds, and in a second commit says when another app holds UDP port 2021 so nothing can be heard. Its no-model harness check against the real P1S passed at 07:30 on 2026-11-01. What nobody has checked is the actual problem: whether a live model, given these new tool results, now tells the person the truth. Kenneth's constraints: live-model runs cost money and are approved one batch at a time (this is one chat); the app must report observations, never guesses; Developer Mode guidance is out of scope until tested on the printer; changes to OrcaSlicer-owned files stay small. Actually connecting the printer (turning LAN Only on at the printer) is a later, separate test.

Task:
Run exactly one live-model chat, with a Sonnet model, through JusPrin's printer chat against Kenneth's real Bambu Lab P1S, and report word for word what the model tells the person. The printer is powered on at 192.168.0.198 in cloud mode (LAN Only off), and it stays that way: do not ask Kenneth to change anything on the printer. Kenneth approved this one chat and no other live-model run.

Code under test: branch `claude/festive-lederberg-693438`, two commits (`ff2fee4fbd`, `ff10faa501`) on top of `jusprin-newui` at `69780c7af4`. Check that branch out in your own worktree. Never touch or build in `/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/.claude/worktrees/festive-lederberg-693438`: another session owns it and has temporarily put pre-fix code back there.

How to drive it: `tests/shell/shell_harness.cpp` has a `--printer-live` mode (documented near line 167, implemented from `begin_printer_live()` near line 3832) that opens the real printer panel with a live model, sends scripted words as the page would, prints every exchange as `HARNESS LIVE` lines, and checks outcomes. It takes `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` or `OPENAI_API_KEY` from the environment and `JUSPRIN_LIVE_MODEL` for the model; use a Sonnet model (`claude-sonnet-5-5`). Add one scenario flag beside it (say `--printer-live-p1s`) that: copies the real Bambu network plug-in from `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/plugins` into the run's throwaway data directory (the `--printer-network-check` scenario on that branch does this; follow it), saves a Bambu Lab P1S printer, opens its Connect chat, and plays the person from the 2026-10-31 incident: ask to connect the printer, and when asked, give the address 192.168.0.198. Wait at least 20 seconds after the first `printer_connection_status` call so the app's note about the printer it saw can reach the model, then send one more line like "so what do I do now?". Print the model's words, every tool call with its result, and the note. Check mechanically: `printer_connection_status` was called; no `printer_connect` succeeded; the model's words name the P1s as seen with LAN Only off and do not claim that no printer is on the network or invent a menu path as fact. Commit the scenario on your branch; keep the run's output and your reading of it in an untracked note at the worktree root (never commit it).

Before the run: `lsof -nP -iUDP:2021` must print nothing (Kenneth's JusPrin, pid 85053 earlier, must be quit; two listeners on that port hide the printer from each other), and no `JusPrinShellHarness` from the other session may be running against the printer (`pgrep -fl JusPrinShellHarness`); wait for it to finish rather than run alongside. Get the API key from Kenneth's `~/Library/Application Support/JusPrin2/JusPrin2.conf` (`/jusprin_agent/...` keys) into the environment without ever printing it; if there is no Anthropic key there and only an OpenRouter one, add the few lines that let the scenario write the OpenRouter provider and key into the throwaway config instead, and use OpenRouter's Sonnet model. Build the harness target only, with `-j4`, after checking `uptime` and `pgrep -fl ninja`; the memory file `/Users/kenneth/.claude/projects/-Users-kenneth-Projects-JusPrin/memory/jusprin-worktree-build.md` has the configure line that reuses the existing deps. Failed runs leave a key-holding throwaway data directory: delete only yours.

Done means: the scenario is committed on your branch, the chat ran once against the real P1S with Sonnet, and your report quotes the model's every message, lists the tool calls and the note with their timing, and says plainly whether the model told the person the truth about the printer (seen at 192.168.0.198, LAN Only off) and what to do, or still guessed. Do not merge any branch, do not push, and do not run a second live chat for any reason.

The live model told the person the truth in the one approved chat against the real P1S: it said the printer was found at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off. It also said connecting is optional and that LAN Only is turned on in the printer's network settings. The scenario is committed on `claude/printer-live-p1s` (`a897a3cbbd`, `5f3bd2e59a`), with nothing merged or pushed, and the printer wasn't changed.

The chat ran at 09:01:48–09:02:46. The provider was Anthropic and the model `claude-sonnet-5-5`; the evidence for the model is the run's app config, because the app's log doesn't record the model name.

## Everything said in the chat
Times are seconds after the chat opened. The opening line comes from the page, not from a model request.

**+0s, page's opening:**
> Let's connect Bambu Lab P1S. Is it turned on, in LAN mode, and on the same network as this computer?
> Choices: Yes, it is | How do I check?

**+0s, person:** Connect my printer

**+9s, model:**
> I'm searching your network for the P1S now. This can take about 15 seconds.

**+21s, app note:**
> The network search has listened for 15 seconds and has found no printer of this model. The app posts another note if one appears.

**+25s, model:**
> The app didn't find your P1S on the network. LAN mode may be turned off on the printer, or the printer may be on a different network from this computer.
> On the printer's screen, open the network settings and look for "LAN Only" mode. Is it turned on?
> Choices: Yes, it's on | No, it's off | I can't find it

**+31s, app note:**
> The network search found P1s at 192.168.0.198 with LAN Only off, which cannot be connected as it is. Connecting it is the person's choice, and the printer prepares prints without a connection.

**+34s, model:**
> Your P1S was found at 192.168.0.198, but LAN Only is off on it, so I can't connect it as it is. To connect it here, you would turn LAN Only on, on the printer's network settings screen. You don't have to, because the printer can prepare prints without a connection.
> Do you want to turn on LAN Only and connect it?
> Choices: I turned LAN Only on | Leave it for now

**+37s, person:** It's at 192.168.0.198

**+41s, model:**
> Thanks. I see it at that address, but it's still in cloud mode, with LAN Only off. I can only connect it once LAN Only is on. You'd turn that on in the printer's network settings.
> Do you want to turn it on and try again, or leave it for now?
> Choices: I turned LAN Only on | Leave it for now

**+44s, person:** so what do I do now?

**+46s, model:**
> You have two options:
> 1. **Connect it:** On the printer's screen, open the network settings and turn on LAN Only. Then tell me, and I'll look for it again. You'll type the access code into a form on this computer, not in this chat.
> 2. **Leave it:** The printer can prepare prints without a connection. You can connect it later from Connect… in its menu on Home.
> Which do you want?
> Choices: I turned LAN Only on | Leave it for now

## Tool calls
The only tool called was `printer_connection_status`, four times, and all four succeeded. The model never called `printer_connect`.

| Time | Search state | Printers in `seen` |
|---|---|---|
| +6s | `started` (0 s) | none |
| +8s | `started` (1 s) | none |
| +22s | `listening` (16 s) | none |
| +38s | `listening` (32 s) | `P1s`, 192.168.0.198, `cloud_mode` |

## Mechanical checks
- **Passed:**
  - The status tool was called.
  - No connect succeeded.
  - The words name the P1S and LAN Only.
  - The words don't claim there is no printer.
- **Failed, but a false alarm:** the no-menu-path check matched "Connect… in its menu on Home", which is a real app menu named in the app's own prompt. I narrowed the word list in `5f3bd2e59a`. The new list compiles and passes on this saved transcript, but hasn't run live.
- **Run result:** the run itself ended `HARNESS RESULT FAIL failures=1` because of that one check.

## Where the chat still falls short
- **Early "didn't find":** at +25s the model said "The app didn't find your P1S" and sent the person to check the printer, 6 seconds before the printer was heard. That was accurate at that moment and hedged, but it doesn't say the search is still running. The app's 15-second note prompted it.
- **Misleading sentence from the app:** "the printer can prepare prints without a connection" comes from the app's own wording (`kPersonsChoice` in `PrinterConversation.cpp`). It's the app that prepares prints, not the printer.
- **Not tested in this chat:**
  - No model read the new `printer_connect` refusal text.
  - "Network settings" comes from the tool description and wasn't checked on the printer.
  - The model didn't ask for the address, so the script volunteered it.

## An unexplained miss before the chat
I ran the free no-model check twice with this new build. The first run, around 08:57, heard nothing for 120 seconds while reporting `listening`. A plain listener on the same Mac at 09:00 heard the printer three times in 45 seconds, and the second run heard it at 25 seconds. I don't know the cause; my unverified guess is macOS's Local Network permission on a new program's first run. If a real person hit this, the app would report `listening` while hearing nothing.

The port was free and no other harness was running at launch, and the API key didn't appear in the output. I deleted this run's data directory, which held the key.

The note with the full tool results is `p1s-live-chat-2026-11-01.md` at the root of the `printer-live-p1s` worktree (untracked), with a copy in the shared notes folder.
